title: Experiment: the running application follows an attestation change on disk
summary: The project view was built with `next build` and served with `next start` on loopback. The route built as `ƒ /` — dynamic — where it had been `○` static before it read anything. Served initially it reported `data-vpw-current="none"` and `data-vpw-stages="9"`, showing every gate ready. One stage attestation was then changed on disk through the typed tool — `04-requirement-gaps` / `every-blocking-gap-decided` set to `not-satisfied` — with the server left running and nothing rebuilt. Three seconds later the same URL reported `data-vpw-current="04-requirement-gaps"`, rendered NOT READY, and named the blocking criterion. Reverting the file returned the page to `data-vpw-current="none"`.

omissions.reason: The page was re-requested by hand. Whether a change reaches an OPEN page without a request is the change stream's job (TSK-0011, TSK-0017) and nothing here shows it.
Deliberately not built in this task — they are TSK-0016's, and they are the half of this view that fails silently. Nothing about them was rendered, so nothing about them was measured.

notes: ⚠️ `ƒ` VERSUS `○` IS THE OBSERVABLE THAT MATTERS. Before this task `/` read nothing and built static; it now builds dynamic because the read awaits `connection()`. A route that had been frozen into the build would have kept serving `none` after the file changed — which is exactly the AST-0019 failure, and exactly what DEC-0019's contract exists to prevent. ⚠️ THE REVERT IS PART OF THE MEASUREMENT. A page that changed once could have been showing anything; changing back on the way out is what makes it a function of the file.
